beats.text: The web was free from the start.
beats.note: It was proposed in 1989. It was not declared free until 1993.

beats.name: Tim Berners-Lee
beats.role: Wrote the proposal at CERN in March. By Christmas 1990 he had written the first browser, editor and server software.

beats.text: It ran on a NeXT computer at CERN.
beats.note: Its address was info.cern.ch, which CERN still hosts as a restored copy of the first site.
CERN put the World Wide Web software in the public domain. That was over four years after the proposal.

beats.text: A later release used an open licence.
beats.note: Both CERN pages say so. Neither names the licence, so this reel does not.

beats.text: Open was a decision, not a default.
